st: Simulating smells, generating the web live and other Paprika

sec.p: Some neuroscientific theories say that the reality out there is entirely a construction of the brain. After all, if you think about it, it's a cluster of neurons and water shut inside a skull, trying to make sense of the various electrical stimuli reaching it. It tries to build…

It's a theme close to our hearts. Dreams, another kind of mental simulation, feed this confusion, as we saw in 🎼 ff.118 Paprika and massages. In the film Paprika, a device, the DC Mini, made it possible for the first time to control a patient's dreams (or reality?). The DC…

Speaking of mental stimulation (and illusions), let's go back to video games for a triple somersault of real/recreated/physical/digital. Reality (COVID) had entered the digital world when we saw Minecraft characters “out of breath”. It was a project to raise awareness of the…

The examples of applications, therapeutic ones included, don't end here. Sabi, a company funded by Khosla and by OpenAI's VP of science Kevin Weil, is trying to read thoughts by developing a ChatGPT of neural patterns. And Motif Neurotech is one of the first companies to get…

Yes, I know, you're thinking it too: yet another technology that solves a “problem” with the “pill” approach. To fix modern depression, it would be enough to remove social media, instead of electronically massaging the brain: a Stanford study on 35,000 people reduced depression…
